title: What is Free Ad Supported TV (FAST) Advertising? 2026 Guide | Strategus

facts.fact: The page states that the average household juggles seven streaming services and spends more on them than it did on cable.
facts.quote: The average household now juggles seven streaming services, spending more than they ever did on cable.

facts.fact: The page states that Tubi amassed 80 million monthly users; the page gives no source or date for this figure.
facts.quote: Tubi quietly amassed 80 million monthly users by offering something radical: free content with commercial breaks.

facts.fact: The page defines FAST as a category of streaming services that deliver a predetermined lineup of video content without requiring a paid subscription.
facts.quote: FAST is a category of streaming services that deliver a predetermined lineup of video content without requiring a paid subscription.

facts.fact: The page says the FAST broadcast model generates its revenue entirely from commercials.
facts.quote: This broadcast model generates revenue entirely from commercials

facts.fact: The page says AVOD is click-to-play on-demand video, while FAST channels follow a broadcast schedule.
facts.quote: AVOD describes click-to-play video content, whereas FAST channels are constrained by a broadcasting schedule.

facts.fact: The page says Hulu is better labeled hybrid video on demand (HVOD) because it earns revenue from both advertisements and monthly subscription fees.
facts.quote: it generates revenue from both advertisements and monthly subscription fees.

facts.fact: The page states that FAST commercials are bought through programmatic auctions, the same way most CTV campaigns are run.
facts.quote: These commercials are purchased via programmatic auctions, the same way most CTV advertising campaigns are executed today.
